items.t: Said a serious investment in career and technical education is necessary to address workforce issues and give young people hard skills.

items.t: Sponsored LD 1025, An Act To Prohibit the Provision of Conversion Therapy to Minors by Certain Licensed Professionals, which Governor Janet Mills signed into law.
items.q: LD 1025, An Act To Prohibit the Provision of Conversion Therapy to Minors by Certain Licensed Professionals, sponsored by Assistant House Majority Leader Ryan Fecteau

items.t: Introduced a bill intended to grow affordable housing options in Maine, which passed the House with bipartisan support, 78-51.
items.q: A bill from Speaker Ryan Fecteau of Biddeford intended to grow affordable housing options in Maine was voted on by the House today. The bill passed with bipartisan support, 78-51.

items.t: Sponsored LD 2003, "An Act To Implement the Recommendations of the Commission To Increase Housing Opportunities in Maine by Studying Zoning and Land Use Restrictions," which allows Maine property owners to build accessory dwelling units in residential areas and up to two units on a lot zoned for single-family housing.
items.q: sponsored by Speaker Fecteau, allows Maine property owners to build accessory dwelling units in residential areas and up to two units on a lot zoned for single-family housing.

record.t: Proposed an initiative to improve dental health access for Maine adults with low incomes, which was funded in the biennial budget passed by the Legislature.
record.q: It includes funding to improve dental health access for Maine adults with low incomes, an initiative from Speaker Ryan Fecteau to shift Maine's reliance on emergency-only dental coverage to a preventative dental care model

record.t: Served as Speaker of the Maine House of Representatives from 2020 to 2022.
record.q: Prior to joining GOPIF, Ryan served as Speaker of the Maine House Representatives from 2020 to 2022.

record.t: Served as Assistant Majority Leader and as Chair of the Committee on Labor, Commerce, Research, and Economic Development.
record.q: He also served as the Maine House Assistant Majority Leader and as Chair of the Committee on Labor, Commerce, Research, and Economic Development during his terms in the Maine Legislature from 2014 to 2022.

record.t: Sponsored legislation to allow Maine's 28 CTE schools to make investments in equipment and capital projects.
